subject: Private VPC: ops checklist, IP allowlist & procurement next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@cloudcore.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC: ops checklist, IP allowlist & procurement next steps

Hi Maya — great to meet today. Quick recap from our call and the minimal artifacts we need to get your Private VPC deployment scheduled. I summarized options and proposed timeline below so your networking and procurement teams can triage.

Summary of deployment modes we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live but not suitable given your data residency/segmentation requirements.
- Dedicated capacity: good middle ground if you want predictable throughput without managing network egress; still requires some allowlist work for egress to Redwood endpoints.
- Private VPC (recommended for CloudCore): private control plane + VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink to keep traffic inside your network. This is what we scoped during the call.

Network deliverables we need from CloudCore (priority order):
1) Decision: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering (we can run over PrivateLink if you prefer no route table changes; peering gives lower latency).
2) Egress IP allowlist: list of CIDRs (or request we provide egress IP set).
3) Certificate and DNS plan: whether you'll provide private hosted zone or we should use a TLS cert for the endpoint.
4) Firewall/proxy details: will connections originate from a NAT gateway, proxy appliance, or managed egress?
5) Connectivity maintenance window preferences for initial cutover.

Procurement & timeline notes:
- We’ll need a signed SOW and PO to reserve Dedicated nodes or to start Private control plane provisioning — typically a 2–3 week lead after procurement clears.
- If you want to fast-track, share a target PO date and we’ll prioritize the capacity reservation.

Next steps (action items):
- Maya: confirm PrivateLink vs Peering and share target procurement date.
- Networking: send egress IPs or allowlist requirements (we can provide our recommended list).
- Security: let us know if you need SOC2 / audit artifacts before kickoff; we attached a short evidence pack.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_requirements.pdf (short checklist), redwood-private-deploy-sla.docx (SLA summary).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Lauren to handle IP/peering specifics once you confirm the option.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_vpc_requirements.pdf (PDF, 210KB)]

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@cloudcore.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:36:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private VPC: ops checklist, IP allowlist & procurement next steps

Thanks Aditya — helpful summary. A few answers from our side and one request for clarification: 

1) PrivateLink vs Peering: our security team prefers PrivateLink to avoid route-table changes across multiple accounts. Could you confirm latency delta vs peering for a typical 1kRPS workload?
2) Procurement timeline: procurement is targeting a PO by 2027-08-25 (two weeks). We’d like to align provisioning to that date.
3) Egress IPs: we can accept a provided list (preferred) rather than publishing our own. If you can send the recommended IP/CIDR set, we’ll route to our firewall team.
4) Certificates/DNS: we will host a private zone in Route53 for the endpoint; we’ll need details on the CN and whether Redwood needs to manage cert rotation.

Also, please confirm who our day-to-day networking contact at Redwood will be so we can start the allowlist ticket internally.

-Maya
Maya Singh
CloudCore Solutions — Platform Ops

Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: ops checklist, IP allowlist & procurement next steps

Thanks Maya — that timeline works. Answering your items and assigning points-of-contact: 

- Latency: PrivateLink typically adds ~2–6 ms compared to peering at similar region/availability zone parity; peering is lower latency but requires cross-account route changes. For typical chat/gen workloads at ~1k RPS we’ve seen median tail 95th token latency increase by ~4ms on PrivateLink in our benchmarks — happy to share the test artifacts if helpful.

- Egress IPs: we’ll provide the recommended egress CIDR set. Lauren, can you prepare the conservative list (and a compact CSV) that CloudCore can drop into their firewall ticket?

- DNS/certs: if you host a private zone we’ll supply the endpoint name and manage a cert on our side; cert rotation will be handled by Redwood unless you prefer to upload and rotate the cert yourselves. Soojin — flag any compliance implications for CloudCore hosting the zone vs Redwood-managed certs.

Immediate asks for our internal team: 
- Lauren: generate 'proposed-network-ips.csv' and confirm PrivateLink endpoint prefix; include both IPv4/IPv6 rows if available.
- Soojin: confirm whether handing certs to customer changes evidence we must produce for the SOC2 / audit package.
- Vivek: FYI — procurement target 2027-08-25; please advise if we should reserve capacity before PO clears to meet a tight go-live.

Maya — once Lauren shares the CSV I’ll send a short one-page allowlist request you can drop into your firewall ticket.

—Aditya
[Attachment: proposed-network-ips.csv will be provided by Lauren]
